hypothesis: Column-wise resampling of parallel tool traces will destroy shared-incident dependence, understate p95 total tool occupancy, and can move critical-path latency in the opposite direction from capacity risk.
claimBoundary: The study identifies estimator behavior under declared stochastic tool-latency distributions and matched replay policies. It does not estimate a named provider, prove a universal bias direction, or model retries, queueing, token generation, serial tool dependencies, or causal production incidents.

baselines: row-preserved replay of the identical generated workflow trace
controls: independent per-tool incidents with the same marginal incident probability
incident-stratified shuffle ablation that retains the observed shared incident label
